content.thinking:
I need to write this module carefully in one pass without testing, so I'm planning the API design first. I'll use a plain-object prop group with a root joint at the origin, since parts without an explicit joint likely need to resolve against some root to avoid errors.

I'm also mapping out moving parts like a chest lid hinge, and deciding to mostly build with simple box parts using tiled textures, reserving lathe shapes for barrels with a carefully designed non-self-intersecting profile. For the barrel surface I'm working out a cell-paint approach that darkens seams between staves based on angular segments to fake a wood-plank look.

For the hoops I'm choosing cylinder geometry sized slightly larger than the barrel radius at each height to simulate iron bands, and now I'm planning out the texture tiles I need overall -- wood planks with nail details, cracked stone tiles for the floor, and a base plinth sized to fit everything together.

Now I'm working out the floor's vertical placement: thin stone slabs roughly 0.5x0.06x0.5 with random offsets, bottom resting at y=0 so the model's 2% sink margin stays negligible against the ~1.5 overall height. Then I'm laying out the scene positions -- floor spanning 2.6 by 2.2, chest toward the back-left, spike trap near the front, and barrels clustered at the back right.

Now I'm placing the remaining props: a fallen barrel, standing torches on iron brazier-stands, and a low back wall of stone bricks (2.6 wide, 1.4 tall, 0.2 thick) sitting at z=-1.0 on top of the floor to hold mounted wall torches alongside the standing ones, keeping proportions consistent with the floor's z-span of roughly -1.1 to 1.1. I'm defining a reusable box-creation helper that takes size, color, and placement options and always attaches parts to the root bone.

For the chest, I need to be careful that parts default to the nearest joint rather than root when there are two joints (root and lid) — so I'm explicitly assigning bone:root to body parts and bone:lid to lid parts. I'm setting up the lid hinge joint at the back of the chest with proper orientation, then using a pose call afterward to rotate the lid open about the hinge axis, working out the correct rotation direction so the front of the lid lifts upward rather than down.

For the lid's curved top, I'm trying to combine a box with a half-cylinder arch, but getting the cylinder's axis and rotation to align properly along X is proving awkward, so I'm considering using a full cylinder instead and letting it get partially embedded in the box.

Actually, simpler to go with a stacked box design instead: a wider flat box for the lid base topped with a slightly narrower box, giving that blocky stepped pixel-art look rather than fighting cylinder orientation. I'm positioning this lid relative to its hinge point at the back top of the chest body, with the body itself spanning a fixed height range in local model space.

I'm adding iron bands and rivets around the body, plus a gold lock plate with a pixel-art keyhole texture on the lid front, while piling small coin and gem shapes onto the open top surface of the chest.

Now moving to the wall torch: an iron bracket with a back plate, arm, and cup holding a wooden cylinder stick with a cloth-wrapped head, and a flame built from stacked, rotated glow boxes in orange, yellow, and white layering for a pixel-flame look, possibly swapped for double-sided flame cards for better visibility.

For standing torches, I'm planning a tripod-style iron brazier or a stone pedestal base with a leaning torch stick and iron ring, placing a couple wall torches, and adding a fallen, charred unlit torch on the floor for variety.

For barrels, I'm setting up three: two upright using a lathe profile at normal height and one tipped on its side using an angled lathe axis, with the top lid colored as dark wood based on surface normal.

For the upright barrel's rim, I'm adding hoop cylinders and seam lines using a modulus pattern on the surface coordinates to break up the plank texture realistically.

Now I'm shaping the barrel profile as a curve that bulges slightly in the middle and narrows at the ends, defining radius values at several y-points to get that classic barrel silhouette.

I'm also considering adding a small decal, like a skull-and-crossbones, as a flat textured plane placed just outside the barrel's surface at its widest point, facing outward.

I'll place the decal near the barrel surface, offsetting slightly outward so it sits visibly on the mesh. For the skeleton pile, I'm planning a skull built from a boxy cranium and jaw with dark eye sockets, using a texture sheet for teeth detail.

I'll add femurs as rods with knob ends, a simplified ribcage made from arced box segments, scattered vertebrae boxes, and small bone fragments, all shaded with variations of a bone-tan color. The pile sits toward the front left, with the skull positioned near the spike trap area to suggest a past victim.

For the spike trap itself, I'm designing a stone pressure plate with a 4x4 grid of holes, each holding a small iron pyramid spike (low-segment cones) tipped with blood-red color, and dark inset squares marking the holes above the floor surface.

I'm adding a skull impaled on the center spike for a gruesome detail, plus thin dark-red blood splat boxes scattered near the trap, carefully offset in height to avoid z-fighting with the floor. Then I'm laying out the floor as a 5x4 grid of stone slabs with small gaps revealing a darker base layer underneath, varying tile heights slightly for texture.

Still working out tile sizing...

I'll build the wall from 0.52x0.52 blocks totaling 1.30 height across two full rows plus a cropped top row, then draw the brick courses with alternating row offsets to get a realistic staggered pattern.

Since the faces are whole tiles, random pixel offsetting won't matter much—better to just use two distinct brick texture variants (BRICKA/BRICKB) for variety. I'll also add thin dark green moss boxes near the wall's lower portion as separate geometry rather than trying to paint it into the texture.

Now I'm positioning wall sconces against the front wall face, then adding cobweb details as small pixel-art planes tucked into the upper corners near the wall, offset slightly outward to avoid z-fighting. I'm also considering a hanging chain made of alternating small boxes draped down the wall.

Then I'm layering in extra flavor props: a melted candle on top of the barrel, scattered gold coin boxes and glowing gem shapes near the chest, a tiny key, and a standing iron torch with a tripod base built from rods and posts.

Now I'm working out exact scene coordinates - placing the back wall torches, positioning the chest with its hinge, and spacing the upright barrels so they don't overlap or spill past the room bounds.

Checking the fallen barrel's position against the spike trap and bones pile for overlaps, both look clear. I'm also verifying the torch placement near the chest and overall height stays under the wall limit, then defining the barrel's lathe radius profile as a function of height.

Now I'm keeping the flat color palette small since colors count toward the limit while textures and paints don't, so I'll define a compact set of palette constants and start writing helper functions for building parts.

Setting up the builder and basic geometry helpers...

Writing wood plank texture...

Working through texel density for the chest body—at 0.7m wide I need the tile sized so planks stay proportional, so I'm testing a 48x32 tile with 0.016 texel scale, giving roughly 44px coverage for the front face. With plank rows at 6px (0.096m each), the chest body's 22px height yields about 3.7 planks, which feels like a reasonable board width.

I'm settling on row height 7 within a 48x35 tile (five rows), applying the same 0.016 texel uniformly across all wood surfaces including barrels, since the painted area density works out to roughly 16mm per cell—plenty of texel resolution. For stone, I'm using a 32x32 tile at the same texel scale, giving slabs with cracked edges and a top-left highlight bevel applied consistently across all faces, then starting to define a stone color ramp for shading. Writing color ramp array...

Still writing tile code...

Still designing pixel patterns...

For bones, I'm building a helper that draws the rod shaft plus small chunky knob boxes at both endpoints, making sure to bind everything to the root bone so joints don't attach to the wrong part.

For the rib cage, I'm thinking of using swept polyline arcs for each rib, curving them up over the spine at intervals to suggest a chest cavity resting on the floor.

Designing the spike trap mechanism now: a stone frame border around a dark pit, with a 4x4 grid of iron spikes at varying heights to look like some are raised and some retracted.

Writing per-spike paint logic...

I'm also considering whether to add a skull impaled on the center spike, but that risks the spike poking through oddly, so maybe placing a skull lying beside the spikes instead is simpler.

Now I'm sketching barrel variations: one upright with lid planks and a candle, another with its lid ajar revealing a glowing green liquid inside, treating it like a wine barrel with a rim detail above the main shape.

I'm adding a spigot and wine puddle to the floor, plus a fallen third barrel spilling dark liquid, and considering simple skull/X decals for each barrel while figuring out decal placement and orientation on the surfaces.

Designing skull pixel art texture...

Now I'm working out the torch geometry — a wall-mounted iron plate with rivets and an angled wooden stick holder, plus a small lathed iron cup to hold the flame.

Writing flame texture rows...

Verifying all 11 pixel rows are 8 characters wide, then moving on to setting up flame cards with billboard orientation and cross-shaped geometry for the fire effect.

I'm adding glowing effects to the flame meshes and small ember cubes scattered near each torch, then considering whether to add soot stain marks on the wall above each torch using thin dark boxes for a weathered look.

I'm also designing a hanging chain on the wall using alternating iron-colored link boxes rotated to simulate 3D links, plus shackle and cuff pieces at the ends, and I'm weighing whether to add a tattered banner with an emblem to the wall as well.

For the banner, I'm planning a thin textured box with a pixel-drawn cloth pattern: red fabric with gold trim, a notched swallowtail cut at the bottom for the tattered look, and a skull emblem stamped in the center, hung from an iron rod with finials, positioned on the wall behind the standing torch so both remain visible.

I'm now working out positions for the rest of the wall props -- shifting the banner, chest, chains, barrels, and second wall torch so they're spaced without overlapping, making sure each torch sits above its nearby prop for good lighting coverage, and placing the standing torch and hanging chain close together without colliding.

Then I'm figuring out the floor layout: spilled coins and a gem near the chest's front, and computing a grid of floor tiles across x and z so they tile the full room footprint and sit flush beneath the walls without gaps.

I'm adding a dark base box beneath the floor tiles for depth, then starting on the chest itself—planning the wooden body dimensions, base trim, and iron bands/corner posts for a dungeon-style look.

Positioning the chest body's center and depth, then sketching out the top rim as an iron frame with the plank body filling the interior space below it.

Adding more coin pile details...

Now I'm positioning the lid as a hinged assembly, stacking progressively narrower boxes above the chest's back rim to create a stepped arch, then planning iron bands across the lid's surface for the pixel-art look.

Setting the hinge joint for the lid with axis pointing sideways, I work out the rotation sign so a -30° angle lifts the front of the lid upward and backward around the hinge, checking that the resulting top point stays within the bounding geometry.

Checking clearance against the back wall: the hinge sits close to the wall, so I trace how a point above the hinge shifts in z as the lid tilts open, confirming it swings backward without intersecting the wall surface.

Now I'm planning the hardware details -- corner iron brackets as thin vertical posts near the chest's four corners, plus a horizontal belt band wrapping around the front at a lower height, sized to sit just outside the main box surface for a studded-iron look.

I'm picking a dark iron color with lighter rivet accents, planning small cube rivets along the belt bands, and adding simple corner feet beneath the base, with a wider trim box as the chest's base plinth in a darker wood tone.

Still writing lathe shading logic...

I'm adding mossy patches near the base using noise sampling, then placing four iron hoops at symmetric vertical offsets near each end of the barrel with slightly expanded radius for the cylinder bands.

For the tilted barrel variant, I'm computing hoop centers by offsetting along the barrel's axis vector rather than straight vertical, so the rings stay perpendicular to the barrel surface. I'm also deciding to add top/bottom rim bands as extra hoops around y=±.235 where the radius is close to .197, to give the barrel a finished chime-ring look before moving on to the candle barrel variant.

Now I'm placing a candle on top of one barrel: a small cream wax cylinder with a wax puddle box beneath and a flame card above the wick, positioned relative to the barrel's top surface. For the other barrel, I'm adding an iron tap assembly made of short rods forming the spigot and spout, a small handle box, and a wine puddle made of overlapping dark red boxes on the floor beneath the tap to suggest a spill. I'm about to start figuring out the position and radius for a third, fallen barrel.

For the fallen barrel I'm computing its tilted axis and extent, considering adding a couple of broken stave planks nearby but skipping loose coins for now. I'm also checking that the bones pile, standing torch, trap, and fallen barrel don't overlap in their x/z footprints -- confirming the torch at roughly (-1.15, 0.05) clears the chest's front edge. Now I'm building the standing iron torch itself: a square base plate, a vertical post rod with collar rings at two heights, a lathed cup near the top, a wood-and-cloth torch head box, and flame elements sitting above it.

I'm sketching a cobweb texture for the top-left wall corner using a pixel grid that draws radial lines and concentric arcs from the origin, then placing it on a plane oriented so the web's corner matches the wall corner, deciding to skip mirroring it for the right corner for now.

Now I'm laying out the wall torch geometry: positioning the plate, stick, and cloth-wrapped head at precise offsets from the wall, angling the rod outward, and adding flame cards at the top so total model height lands around 1.55 units. I'm also sketching an iron collar bracket near the base of the stick to hold it in place.

For the standing torch, I'm setting flame and head positions relative to the post top, then planning ember glow effects using small randomly-placed boxes and emissive glow on the gems. I'm also designing pixel-dithered torchlight pools -- warm-colored planes with bayer dithering to fake a circular glow -- placed just above the floor tiles to avoid z-fighting, and considering a similar wall-facing glow plane for the wall-mounted torches.

Now I'm checking the exact z-depths of the wall halo plane, torch plate, and banner box to make sure they layer correctly against the wall without overlapping or z-fighting.

Defining the color palette constants...

Still defining color palette...

I'm making sure the total flat color count stays under 64, then adding a helper function to scatter small moss patches with randomized size and spread across the terrain.

Now I'm setting up the file imports and tools needed to build the scene: geometry utilities, pixel art helpers, noise/paint functions, and glow effects.

Setting up the build function with a seeded RNG and joint-based root, now defining box geometry helpers...

Still writing floor tile layout, but I need to double check the back row's z-range against the wall position to avoid overlap.

Now I'm laying out the wall itself: computing column x-centers, row y-centers and heights, and alternating brick textures per tile with a consistent depth, then considering adding a crenellated coping along the top row.

For the top edge, I'm giving alternating columns taller vs shorter heights to form merlons. I'm also placing torches between columns on the wall face, webs in the top corners, and figuring out positions for banners and corner decorations above the main wall height.

For the halo texture I'm generating a radial pixel pattern with a soft golden falloff plus a brighter inner ring, leaving the outside transparent, then applying it as a glowing plane positioned just behind the wall.

Now I'm writing the skull function, building a cranium box textured with the skin material and positioning a jaw piece beneath it, computing the jaw's offset by rotating a local center vector by the skull's yaw so it sits correctly under the cranium.

I'm working out the vertical stacking so the jaw rests on the floor and the cranium sits directly on top of it, aligning the cranium's bottom with the jaw's top surface to compute each piece's center y-coordinate.

For skinning the skull texture I'm deciding to skip glowing eye details since the cranium's pixel texture can't be shaded separately, and now I'm writing the fill logic that colors each face rectangle using a bone-tone ramp with randomized shading.

Working out eye socket and jaw stamp placement...

I'm sizing the overall skin layout to fit the skull pieces side by side, then shifting to positioning the bones in the pile—figuring out skull, ribcage, and femur placement with rotation angles for a natural scattered look.

Still placing bones...

Still writing rib arc geometry...

Spine rod extended, skipping sternum detail. Now I'm setting up the spike trap with a stone frame border using tiled boxes for the front and back panels.

Adding side panels, pit floor...

I'm defining blood versus steel color ramps for the spike tips, with the paint choice weighted by tip fraction and surface normal direction for lighting variation. I'm checking that the cell size relative to the cone's small radius still gives enough resolution across the spike surface, and confirming the geometry's base dimensions are reasonable for a 4-sided cone.

I'm scattering small blood-stained boxes near the trap floor's pit opening, then placing an impaled skull on one taller spike by calculating the skull's vertical offset so the spike tip sits convincingly inside the cranium.

Now I'm defining a radius function for the barrel's profile that tapers near the top and bottom, then building its outline points across a set of y-values to generate the barrel geometry.

Adding iron hoop bands around the barrel...

Decal placement at y within the hoop bounds should fit fine, and I'll pass `bone: root` to make the decal rigid rather than skinned. For the marks, I'm planning a small set of pixel-art icons—skull, X mark, and a flask/drop design—sketching out the pixel grid and color palette for the flask icon now.

Finishing the pixel X pattern, then moving to gem geometry using octahedrons with flat shading, and merging coins by color using cylinder geometries with slight tilt transforms.

Still writing coin geometry and chest dimensions...

I'm working out the lid's pivot position relative to the hinge, then sizing the corner posts so they protrude slightly beyond the chest body on all sides, and starting to lay out the metal belt bands wrapping around the box.

Switching to vertical iron straps instead, placed symmetrically with small rivet details on their fronts, plus adding a gold lock plate centered on the front face.

Designing keyhole pixel art...

Adding lid rivets, iron bands, and plank textures...

Now placing the coin pile within the rim interior, with spilled coins near the front floor, gems scattered on top, and a goblet resting on the pile for added detail.

I'm defining helper functions for wall and floor torches, setting up tuple types for coordinates, and writing a box helper that accepts size, color, position, and rotation options. I'm also building a moss generation function that scatters small irregular moss patches with randomized size, color, and rotation around a given point.

Now I'm placing moss patches near walls and barrel bases at specific coordinates, making sure they layer correctly above the floor without clipping, then extending this to wall-mounted moss boxes. I'm also sketching out small mushroom clusters near the wall base using stem and cap boxes with reddish coloring.

I'm tallying up the total part count across floor, walls, chest, coins, barrels, trap mechanism, bones, torches, moss, and chains to confirm the scene stays within a reasonable budget—landing around 350 parts. I'm also verifying that the glow function's type signature correctly accepts the Mesh array returned by the card-building helper.

Now I'm writing the torch flame function with embers...

Still writing the wall-mounted torch bracket code, including the iron mount, decorative studs, and the angled rod arm holding it to the wall...

Placing a small flame cap above the stick, then adding a halo plane behind the figure and soot streak boxes above it for atmospheric detail.

Now I'm checking wall torch heights at different mounting positions so the flame tops stay within the wall's bounds, settling on y=.85 for both torches. For the standing torch, I'm building a tripod base with a central post and angled support legs using thin rod geometry.

Still writing torch geometry...

Then I'm adding a floor halo pool plane positioned above the tile surface with the HALO color, sized to spread near the chest area, checking it doesn't visually conflict with bones and moss scattered on the ground.

Next I'm placing a charred fallen torch near the trap, between the chest and barrels, giving it a wooden rod and char-smudged head, then positioning a wall banner near the torch's light halo.

Writing banner texture code...

Still designing cloth colors and border...

Now I'm adding a chain hanging on the wall with shackle links and a manacle cuff near the bottom, alternating box orientations for realism.

I'm also thinking about moss at the wall base, then moving to writing the stone texture generator with a procedural ramp-based fill function.

Writing texture generation code...

Still writing brick tile shading...

Now I'm defining a barrel's cell-painted shading, using lathe coordinates to carve stave grooves and seams, blending in a mossy patch near the base using noise, and picking tones from a barrel color ramp with dithering.

I'm assembling the final piece: sketching the goblet's lathe profile, adding glowing octahedron gems in distinct colors, building rods and swept paths for the frame, and verifying each function's bone, color, and option signatures line up correctly before posing the lid onto the root joint.

Still writing bone pile helpers...

I'm sketching ribcage ribs with sweep curves, scattering small vertebrae boxes with random rotations, and adding thin rod bones for finger details, then wrapping up the color constants object.
